literal: To fatten one's own flesh, oneself another's flesh eats, how will possess compassion?
translation: How can he possess compassion, who eats the flesh of another living being to fatten his own flesh?
modern: தன் உடம்பின் சதையை வளர்ப்பதற்காக, மற்றொரு உயிரினத்தின் உடம்பின் சதையை உண்பவன் எவ்வாறு அருளைப் பெற முடியும்?
explanation: This couplet opens the chapter on abstaining from flesh-eating by questioning the compatibility of meat-eating with compassion. The poet contrasts 'one's own flesh' (தன் ஊன்) with 'another's flesh' (பிறிது ஊன்). To grow one's own body by consuming the body of another sentient being is presented as a fundamental contradiction to the concept of 'aruḷ' (compassion or grace). The rhetorical question 'how will he possess compassion?' emphasizes that true mercy cannot coexist with the act of killing and eating other living creatures for personal nourishment.
